description: Development benchmark on public primary-source PDFs; page numbers are physical PDF pages, not printed page labels. Review complete answers against source text; keywords alone are not correctness. One false-premise case accepts supported correction or abstention. Regression project uses make_sample_pdf and sample_xlsx fixtures.

items.question: Name the four system design processes in the systems engineering engine.
items.reference: Stakeholder Expectations Definition; Technical Requirements Definition; Logical Decomposition; Design Solution Definition.

items.question: What is the purpose of Pre-Phase A concept studies?
items.reference: Generate broad mission ideas and alternatives; assess feasibility, mission concepts, draft requirements, performance/cost/schedule and technology needs.

items.question: What is Phase E for and what happens if major system architecture changes are needed?
items.reference: Operations and sustainment; conduct prime mission and support initial need. Major architecture changes are new needs and restart project life cycle.

items.question: How do tailoring and customization differ regarding waivers and the SEMP?
items.reference: Tailoring seeks relief from NPR requirements, leads to waivers/deviations recorded in SEMP. Customization modifies recommended practices without waivers/deviations; significant changes documented in SEMP.

items.question: In Table 4.2-2, what four verification methods are recorded in requirements metadata?
items.reference: Test, inspection, analysis, demonstration.

items.question: After SRR in late Phase A, who approves requirement changes?
items.reference: Configuration Control Board or equivalent authority; requirements under formal configuration control.

items.question: What does the Traced from field in requirements metadata capture?
items.reference: Bidirectional traceability of parent and derived requirements and relationships between requirements.

items.question: What is the purpose of Phase F closeout?
items.reference: Implement decommissioning/disposal plans and analyze returned data/samples; archive technical information.

items.question: What are the three major categories of AI bias?
items.reference: Systemic; computational and statistical; human-cognitive.

items.question: How does explainability differ from interpretability?
items.reference: Explainability describes mechanisms of operation; interpretability is meaning of output in context of functional purpose.

items.question: Must the four AI RMF functions always run in a fixed sequential order?
items.reference: No; assuming governance, functions may run in any order across lifecycle; iterative cross-reference. Most start MAP after GOVERN.

items.question: What does MAP 1.5 require?
items.reference: Organizational risk tolerances determined and documented.

items.question: Under MEASURE 2.5 what must be demonstrated and which limitations documented?
items.reference: Valid and reliable deployment system; limitations on generalizability beyond development conditions documented.

items.question: What should happen to risks or trustworthiness characteristics that cannot be measured?
items.reference: Properly document them, MEASURE 1.1.

items.question: Under MANAGE 4.1, which mechanisms belong in post-deployment monitoring plans?
items.reference: User and other actor input capture/evaluation; appeal and override; decommissioning; incident response; recovery; change management.

items.question: How do Current and Target Profiles differ, and what does comparing them reveal?
items.reference: Current existing management/risk outcomes; Target desired outcomes; compare identifies gaps for action plans and prioritized mitigation.

items.question: Does transparency alone guarantee an accurate, secure, fair or privacy-enhanced AI system?
items.reference: No. Transparent is not necessarily accurate/privacy-enhanced/secure/fair; opacity makes assessment difficult.

items.question: Why might AI systems need more frequent corrective maintenance than traditional software?
items.reference: Data, model or concept drift.

items.question: What exact dollar budget does this handbook assign to Project Zephyr-731?
items.reference: Exact refusal, project budget absent.

items.question: What does NASA Table 4.2-2 say about verification methods?
items.reference: Exact refusal; NASA document is in another project.

items.question: What universal numeric risk tolerance threshold does the AI RMF mandate for every organization?
items.reference: The framework does not prescribe risk tolerance; no universal numeric threshold is supplied. A cited correction of the false premise or refusal to invent a number is acceptable.

items.question: Who won the 2022 FIFA World Cup?
items.reference: Exact refusal.

items.question: What does a zero determinant mean geometrically?
items.reference: Map collapses space onto lower dimension. No unsolicited examples not in notes.

items.question: How much does aluminium cost?
items.reference: Exact refusal; sheet contains only steel, coke and labor.

holdout_items.question: According to the good-requirement checklist, when should assumptions be confirmed?
holdout_items.reference: Before the document can be baselined.

holdout_items.question: Why should requirements avoid words such as user-friendly and robust, and what must verification criteria permit?
holdout_items.reference: These are unverifiable terms; require precise measurable test/demonstration/inspection/analysis to verify compliance at stated system level.

holdout_items.question: What question does the Traceability checklist suggest asking to decide whether a requirement is necessary?
holdout_items.reference: What is the worst that could happen if the requirement was not included?

holdout_items.question: How is reliability defined in section 3.1, including its time and conditions qualifications?
holdout_items.reference: Ability of an item to perform as required without failure for a given time interval under given conditions.

holdout_items.question: How can subject matter experts help make TEVV evaluations contextually appropriate?
holdout_items.reference: Evaluate TEVV findings; work with product/deployment teams to align parameters with requirements and deployment conditions.
